propositions: On platforms without /proc (macOS), _process_start_time always returns None, making the recycled-pid discriminant unsatisfiable and causing dead processes whose pid numbers were recycled to be incorrectly judged as live holders indefinitely
A stale lock with a live but unrelated pid and no recoverable start time must be reclaimed once the age exceeds the ceiling, not exempted from timing bounds

A genuinely live holder with matching known start times must never be reclaimed on a timer due to the dual-leg invariant: the fcntl.flock leg is held for the entire lifetime of the mkdir leg, so reaching the stale check proves the owner let go
The owner-identity/stamp/staleness/reclaim cluster must be split from lock.py to lock_owner.py to fit module size constraints, with unidirectional dependency and no re-export shim
